newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iraq is fully cooperating with U.N. - Rasheed.
newsitem.headline: Iraq is fully cooperating with U.N. - Rasheed.

text.p: Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Rasheed said on Tuesday that Iraq was fully cooperating with the United Nations and that "hostile forces" were trying to paint a bad image of the Arab country in front of the Security Council.
"Iraq is fully cooperating, has been cooperating and will cooperate because we know it is in Iraq's interest," Rasheed told a news conference during a trip to Spain.

"But there are designs by hostile forces to try to undermine this cooperation between the Iraqi government and the special commission so that for political objectives, Iraq is given a bad image in front of the Security Council," he said.
On Monday, the U.N. Security Council adopted a resolution threatening Iraq with further sanctions if it did not allow arms inspectors to search sensitive sites.

"The result will be that paragraph 22 will be delayed and the embargo will continue and in this way these hostile forces are hoping that the Iraqi community will collapse and the Iraqi regime will be overthrown," Rasheed said.
A U.N. arms official said that while Iraq had shown readiness to cooperate with United Nations weapons inspectors, there was no indication it would allow U.N. teams full access to all sites.
United Nations sanctions were imposed against Iraq in 1990 after its invasion of Kuwait.
